# Why Trust It?

This is the text of the app's **Why Trust It?** help topic and of the dossier its button opens. The claims ledger behind it is [TRUST_CLAIMS.md](TRUST_CLAIMS.md).

**The whole design assumes a qualified person checks every output, so the app never edits your originals, never quietly guesses, and withholds any file it cannot verify.**

- **Your original files are never edited.** The app copies your template and each target to a private snapshot, confirms the copy matches the original by its SHA-256 fingerprint, and works only on the copy. Each original is checked again before its output is published; if it changed during the run, nothing is published for it.
- **Rules decide first, AI only the rest.** A paragraph whose role is proven by Word's own numbering or by unmistakable text such as PART 1 - GENERAL is decided by fixed rules on your computer, and the AI cannot overrule them. Only the remaining paragraphs are sent. When rules settle everything, no request is made at all.
- **The AI picks labels, never your words.** For each paragraph it is shown, the AI may only answer which CSI role it has (PART, ARTICLE, PARAGRAPH and so on) or that it is not CSI content. Formatting is copied from the template's own paragraphs, and no model writes the text of your specification.
- **Nothing is silently dropped or filled in.** Every visible body paragraph outside tables, text boxes and drawings must end up styled or explicitly ignored, exactly once. A gap, a duplicate, or an answer outside the allowed roles fails that target; it is never patched from the paragraph next door.
- **A file that fails a check is withheld.** Before publishing, the app proves the body text is unchanged except where the mode said it would change, and that numbering, tracked changes, indentation and every untouched part of the file survived. A failed check withholds that one output; your other targets still finish.
- **One thing runs without you, and it is named.** About 1.5 seconds after launch, at most once a day, the app asks github.com for a small version file. It sends no document data, no key and no version number. Set SPEC_FORMATTER_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK to turn it off. Every AI request, retries included, happens only inside a run you started.
- **Your key and your spend stay yours.** Requests go straight from your computer to Anthropic (api.anthropic.com) with your own key and are billed to your Anthropic account; no server of this app's sits in between. The key is held in memory, or in Windows Credential Manager if you tick Remember, and is removed from every log and record.
- **Every run leaves a record you can check.** Each run gets its own timestamped folder with run.log, an audit per target, diagnostics.jsonl and run.json: fingerprints of every input and output, the models used, and the tokens counted. None of it holds your paragraph text or your key.

> **Not convinced?** Fair. The points above are claims — here is the mechanism behind each one, action by action, plus how to audit any of it yourself.

<a id="short-answer"></a>

### The short answer

*Start here*

Specification Formatter applies an architect's Word template to your specifications, or converts their numbering between CSI and Canadian CSC PageFormat. Three commitments hold the rest of this document together.

- **Every part of the output has a declared origin.** Your words and, in Format only, your numbering come from your target. Formatting comes from the template's own paragraphs or from the app's built-in Canadian scheme. The AI contributes role labels and, for a template, the names of the styles it generates. One gap: the records say how many paragraphs the AI labelled, not which ones.
- **Nothing runs that you did not start, with one named exception.** The exception is the daily update check, which sends no document data and can be switched off. Template analysis, AI labelling and every retry happen only inside a run you started with FORMAT SPECS.
- **Every automated judgment is checked; the rule-based ones can be re-derived.** Rules give the same answer every time for the same file. AI answers are not guaranteed to repeat, so each one is confined to a fixed list of roles, checked for complete coverage, and then held to the same verification gates as everything else before a file is published.

<a id="provenance"></a>

### Where the output comes from

*Provenance*

| Origin | What it actually is | How you can tell |
|---|---|---|
| Your target specification | All body text apart from the list numbers a conversion changes, plus tables, footnotes, comments, images and tracked changes. In Format only, also its list numbers, levels and restarts. | Format only proves body text and numbering unchanged before publishing. Every part of the file outside the mode's remit is checked byte for byte. In Format only, Word's Review › Compare shows no text changes in the body. |
| The architect template (two template modes) | Paragraph styles copied from the template's own example paragraphs, document defaults, theme, page layout, and headers and footers. In Canadian mode, also its numbering. | run.json records the template's SHA-256 fingerprint. run.log lists every part of the file that changed, was added or was removed. |
| The built-in Canadian scheme (no-template conversion) | A nine-level PART / 1.1 / .1 numbering list generated from constants inside the app and checked against the same rules a template must pass. No styles, fonts or headers are applied. | run.json says numbering_scheme: builtin_csc and records the scheme's fingerprint. |
| Fixed rules in the app | Most role decisions, both Canadian conversions, the numbers written back as typed CSI markers, and the section number and title placed in imported headers. | run.log: “Built slim bundle: N unresolved + M deterministic”. Deterministic means decided by rules. |
| AI, through Anthropic | A role label for each paragraph the rules could not settle. For a newly analyzed template, which paragraph is the example of each role, and the display names of the CSI_ styles it creates; those names appear in Word's Styles pane in the two template modes. | run.log says “Classifying unresolved paragraphs with Anthropic” or “Anthropic request skipped”. run.json records the models, effort and tokens. The audit lists every paragraph's final role, but not whether a rule or the AI chose it. |

> **Things that are not happening**
>
> There is no hidden library or corpus: the only reference material shipped is the classifiers' prompt files and the built-in numbering scheme, and nothing is fetched from the internet to write your output. There is no server, account or sign-in belonging to this app, so nothing is shared between users. The app does no training of its own; Anthropic's Commercial Terms state that “Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services.” There is no telemetry, crash reporting or analytics. The AI never sees a whole document, an image, a header or footer, or a file name.

<a id="engine"></a>

### What the engine actually is

*Engine*

| Job | Model or component | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Analyze a template the app has not seen before | Anthropic Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), on Anthropic's servers: adaptive thinking, effort “high”, at most 128,000 output tokens, no tools. | The most capable model, for a job done once per template version; the result is cached and reused for free. |
| Label target paragraphs that rules could not settle | Anthropic Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) by default, or Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) from the Target AI model menu, on Anthropic's servers: adaptive thinking, effort “high”, at most 128,000 output tokens, no tools. | Haiku is the lower-cost default; Sonnet is there for documents where you want the larger model. |
| Measure template requests and Haiku requests before sending them | Anthropic's token-counting service, on Anthropic's servers. | Enforces the cost limits described under Money. It produces no answer and is not billed as model use. |
| Everything else: copying, unpacking, rules, conversion, styling, checking, packaging, publishing | This app's own code, on your computer. | Deterministic: the same input gives the same result, with no AI and no network. |
| Remember your key (optional) | Windows Credential Manager, on your computer. | Only when you tick Remember. |
| Check for updates | Python's standard web client, talking to github.com. | So you can get fixes; it can be switched off. |

The settings in plain words. Adaptive thinking lets the model decide how much to reason before it answers; effort “high” asks it to be thorough. The output limit stops a runaway answer. No temperature or other randomness setting is sent, and the model is offered no tools, so it can only reply with text. That reply must fit a fixed JSON schema: a machine-checkable form listing exactly which fields and values are allowed.

<a id="boundary"></a>

### What leaves your computer, and where it goes

*The boundary*

```text
[Your computer]
   Your originals (read only)
   Working copies (temporary)
   Outputs and run records
   Template cache
   Key in Credential Manager (optional)
   -----> Anthropic — api.anthropic.com: Only in a run that needs AI: paragraph excerpts + key
   - - -> GitHub — github.com: Automatic, once a day at most: update file, no document data
   - - -> GitHub release download: Only when you click Download & Install: the installer
   (Solid: only in a run that needs AI. Dashed: automatic or on request.)
```

*Data-flow diagram, in words. Your computer holds your original files, the working copies, the outputs and run records, the template cache and, if you chose Remember, your key. One solid arrow leaves it: to Anthropic at api.anthropic.com, only during a run that needs AI, carrying paragraph excerpts and your key. Two dashed arrows are automatic or optional: to github.com at most once a day for a small update file, with no document data; and from GitHub only when you click Download & Install, for the installer.*

**Leaves your machine**

- To api.anthropic.com, only during a run that needs AI: up to 200 characters of each paragraph the rules could not settle, up to 80 characters of the paragraphs before and after it, its style name and numbering and formatting hints, the role list and the app's prompt. For a new template, every template paragraph (up to 200 characters each) with its style and numbering catalogs. Your key travels in the request header.
- Before each such request, the same content to Anthropic's token-counting service on the same host.
- With every Anthropic request, the standard headers of Anthropic's software library: its version, your operating system, processor type and Python version.
- To github.com, automatically at most once a day and whenever you click Check for Updates: one request for a small file named latest.json, identified as SpecificationFormatter-Updater. Like any web request it shows GitHub your IP address.
- From GitHub, only when you click Download & Install: the installer named in that file.
- Through your own browser or mail program, only when you click a link: Anthropic's console, the releases page, the author's LinkedIn page or email address.

**Stays on your machine**

- Your original template and targets, which are only read.
- Whole documents, tables, images, headers and footers, comments and footnotes.
- File names and folder paths.
- Every output and every run record.
- The template cache and the update-check state.
- Your key, if you chose Remember.
- All rule-based decisions, conversions and checks.

> **Settings that can move this boundary**
>
> The environment variable ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, which Anthropic's library honours, sends every AI request, excerpts and key included, to another host instead of api.anthropic.com. SPEC_FORMATTER_UPDATE_URL sends the update check elsewhere (it must still be HTTPS). The app never sets either one and does not show them in the window. If your IT department set one, your traffic goes where they pointed it. Separately, both Anthropic's library and the update check follow your computer's proxy settings, so on a network with a proxy the same requests pass through it on their way to the same hosts.

<a id="runtime"></a>

### What runs when you click

*Runtime*

One card per action, including what happens on its own. Every card answers the same five questions in the same order, so you can compare them. Cards marked automatic run without a click of their own.

#### 1. Opening the app

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Start Specification Formatter. |
| **What runs** | The window is built. The key field is filled from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable if it is set, otherwise from Windows Credential Manager if you chose Remember earlier. The update check (next card) is scheduled. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | If Credential Manager cannot be read, the key field stays empty and nothing else changes. |

#### 2. Automatic update check *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Nothing. It runs about 1.5 seconds after the window opens, if the last check was a day or more ago. |
| **What runs** | A background task downloads latest.json, reads the version, installer address and SHA-256 fingerprint in it, and compares the version with yours on your computer. It writes the time of the check to update_check.json. An Update available window appears only if the version is newer and you have not skipped it. |
| **What is sent** | One HTTPS request to https://github.com/abe-borg/spec-template-normalizer/releases/latest/download/latest.json (GitHub forwards it to its download servers). No document data, key or version number. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | 8-second timeout; reads at most 64 KiB; refuses anything but HTTPS, including after redirects. A failure is silent apart from the footer. SPEC_FORMATTER_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK turns it off. |

#### 3. Check for Updates

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Click Check for Updates in the footer. |
| **What runs** | The same check as the automatic one, then a message with the result. |
| **What is sent** | The same single request to github.com. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | The same timeout, size cap and HTTPS rule. If checks are switched off, it says so and sends nothing. |

#### 4. Download & Install, Later, Skip this Version

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Choose one of the buttons in the Update available window. |
| **What runs** | Download & Install is refused while a run is active. Otherwise the installer is downloaded to a temporary name in %LOCALAPPDATA%\SpecificationFormatter\updates, its SHA-256 fingerprint is checked against latest.json, and only then is it renamed. You are asked once more; yes launches the installer and closes the app. Later closes the window. Skip this Version stops the automatic prompt for that version. The View this release on GitHub link opens the releases page in your browser. |
| **What is sent** | Download & Install: one HTTPS request for the installer address named in latest.json. Later and Skip: nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | At most 512 MiB; 60-second timeout per network read; HTTPS only. A fingerprint mismatch deletes the file, so it can never be run. The installer shows the license page again. Downloaded installers are not deleted afterwards. |

#### 5. Choose File (architect template)

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Click Choose File and pick a .docx. |
| **What runs** | Windows' file dialog. The path is remembered; the file is not opened until you click FORMAT SPECS. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | Disabled in the two no-template modes and during a run. |

#### 6. Add Files, Add Folder, Clear

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Add target files or a folder of them, or clear the list. |
| **What runs** | The preview lists the .docx files directly inside a folder (not in its subfolders), leaving out Word lock files, this app's own outputs, and the architect template. The output folder defaults to a Formatted Specs folder beside the first file, or inside the first folder. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | Only the folder listing is read. Locked during a run. |

#### 7. Choose the output mode and Target AI model

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Pick one of the four modes, and Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5. |
| **What runs** | The two no-template modes grey out the template field. The model choice is stored for the next run. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. (This choice decides which model a later run uses.) |
| **Bounded by** | Both are locked while a run is active. |

#### 8. Output folder

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Type a folder or click Choose Folder. |
| **What runs** | The path is remembered for the next run. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | Every run writes into a new subfolder of it; nothing already there is changed. |

#### 9. API key, Show, Remember, How do I get one?

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Paste a key, tick Show or Remember, or click How do I get one? |
| **What runs** | Show reveals the key in the field. Ticking Remember saves the key to Windows Credential Manager straight away (service SpecificationFormatter, user name anthropic-api-key) and again when a run starts; unticking deletes it. How do I get one? opens a help window whose console link opens in your browser. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. The console link opens https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys in your browser only when you click it. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | If Credential Manager refuses the key, Remember unticks itself and a message says the key will not be remembered. |

#### 10. FORMAT SPECS: checking inputs

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Click FORMAT SPECS. |
| **What runs** | Checks that each input is a saved .docx, not a Word lock file, not one of this app's outputs, and that the template is not also a target. Checks the output folder can be written. Only then creates the run folder <UTC time>_<mode>_<run id> and locks every input on the screen. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | A problem here stops the run before the run folder is created and before anything is sent. |

#### 11. Template step: a template already analyzed *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Run a template mode with a template the app has analyzed before. |
| **What runs** | The template's SHA-256 fingerprint is computed and the cache is searched for a profile with the same fingerprint, app engine, model, prompts and format version. Every file in that profile is checked against its recorded fingerprint, then it is used. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | A damaged or mismatched profile is ignored, never used. If the template changes during the run, the run stops. |

#### 12. Template step: a new or changed template *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Run a template mode with a template the app has not analyzed. |
| **What runs** | The template is copied, unpacked within size limits and read paragraph by paragraph. Its size is estimated and then measured with Anthropic's token counter. One request asks the model to map CSI roles to example paragraphs; up to 3 follow-up requests cover any paragraphs it missed. Fixed rules then correct roles that strong text signals contradict, coverage must be complete, styles are copied from the example paragraphs, the page layout and headers are captured, and a fingerprinted profile is saved to the cache. Older profiles of that template beyond the newest 2 are deleted. In Canadian mode the template's numbering is checked before any target starts. |
| **What is sent** | To api.anthropic.com: every template paragraph (up to 200 characters each) with its style, numbering and formatting hints, the template's style and numbering catalogs, fingerprints of its headers and footers, and the app's two template prompts. The same content goes to the token counter first. |
| **AI involved** | Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5): adaptive thinking, effort “high”, at most 128,000 output tokens, no tools. |
| **Bounded by** | Refused before any request above 150,000 input tokens. 3 attempts in all for network or server errors, with 2- and 4-second waits; 2 attempts for an unusable answer; a refusal is final. Connection timeout 5 seconds, answer timeout 10 minutes. A failure stops the whole run before any target, with records written; tokens already used are billed and recorded. |

#### 13. Template step: the no-template modes *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Run Convert CSI to Canadian - no template, or Convert Canadian back to CSI. |
| **What runs** | For the first, the built-in nine-level Canadian scheme is generated from constants and checked against the same rules a template's numbering must pass. For the second, nothing is needed: numbers are written as text. Nothing is cached. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | A template supplied through the Python interface is refused rather than ignored. |

#### 14. Each target: copy, unpack and rule-based labelling *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Nothing more; this runs for every target. |
| **What runs** | Up to 3 targets are processed at once. Each is copied to a short temporary folder and fingerprinted, unpacked within the size limits, and read paragraph by paragraph with its styles and numbering. Fixed rules label every paragraph whose role Word's numbering or unmistakable text proves. What is left is counted. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | Unpacking: at most 10,000 entries, 512 MiB in all, 128 MiB per part, compression no higher than 1,000 to one. A target with more than 2,000 unlabelled paragraphs fails here, before any request (SPEC_FORMATTER_MAX_TARGET_PARAGRAPHS changes the limit). A failure affects only this target. |

#### 15. Each target: AI labelling of the rest *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Nothing more; this happens only if some paragraphs are still unlabelled. |
| **What runs** | Long targets are split into chunks of about 80,000 estimated tokens or 300 paragraphs, overlapping by 20 paragraphs, up to 6 at once. Each Haiku request is measured with Anthropic's token counter first (Sonnet requests are not). The answer is streamed back and checked: only paragraphs that were sent, each exactly once, each with an allowed role. If two chunks disagree in their overlap, those paragraphs are asked once more. Finally every paragraph must have exactly one answer. |
| **What is sent** | To api.anthropic.com: for each unlabelled paragraph, up to 200 characters of its text, up to 80 characters of its neighbours, its style name and numbering and formatting hints; the role list; the app's target prompt; your key in the header. Table paragraphs are never sent. |
| **AI involved** | Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) by default, or Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) if you chose it: adaptive thinking, effort “high”, at most 128,000 output tokens, no tools. SPEC_FORMATTER_TARGET_EFFORT can change the effort; the app never sets it. |
| **Bounded by** | Each Haiku request must measure under 95,000 tokens, or the target fails before it is sent. At most 4 requests are open at once across the whole run. Network, rate limit and server errors get 2 retries (rate-limit waits capped at 120 seconds); an unusable answer gets 2 more tries; a refusal is final. No key means the target fails here. A failure affects only this target; tokens already used are billed and recorded. |

#### 16. Each target: apply, verify, publish *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Nothing more. |
| **What runs** | The mode is applied. Format only brings in the template's styles without replacing any style your file already has, and applies its page layout, headers and footers while keeping your own numbering. Convert CSI to Canadian removes typed CSI markers and puts the converted paragraphs on the Canadian list (the template's or the built-in one); with a template it also applies the template's styles, layout, headers and footers. Convert Canadian back to CSI writes each number into the text. Then every check runs on the finished file: body text run by run, numbering, tracked changes by author and kind, indentation, styles read back, and every untouched part of the file byte for byte. The original is fingerprinted again, and only then is the file copied into the run folder in one step and its fingerprint confirmed. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | Any failed check means no output for this target, with an error code, a fixed explanation and, where known, the paragraph's location. Your other targets continue. |

#### 17. Writing the run records *(automatic)*

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Nothing more. |
| **What runs** | One audit.json per target, then run.log, diagnostics.jsonl and, last, run.json. Temporary files are removed and a message box reports the result. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |
| **AI involved** | None. |
| **Bounded by** | Written even when some or all targets failed. If writing them fails after outputs were published, a run.json saying so is still written. |

#### 18. Cancel

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Click Cancel during a run. |
| **What runs** | A stop signal is set. No new target or request starts, waits between retries end at once, and an answer still arriving is cut off at its next piece. Targets not yet published are marked cancelled. The run records are written. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing new. |
| **AI involved** | None started. |
| **Bounded by** | Outputs already published stay. Tokens of answers that finished are billed and recorded. An answer cut off midway is recorded as unknown, not zero, and Anthropic may still bill what it produced. |

| | |
|---|---|
| **You do** | Close the window while a run is active. |
| **What runs** | You are asked whether to cancel. Yes cancels as above and closes the window once the records are saved; No keeps the run going. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing new. |
| **AI involved** | None started. |
| **Bounded by** | The same as Cancel. |

|---|---|
| **You do** | Click Open Output Folder. |
| **What runs** | File Explorer opens the folder of the last run. |
| **What is sent** | Nothing. |

|---|---|

<a id="blast-radius"></a>

### What the AI may touch, and what it cannot

*Blast radius*

| Capability | What it can do | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| Label a target paragraph | Give one role to each paragraph it was sent. | The role must be one of the template's role names. Answers about paragraphs it was not sent, duplicates and unknown roles are rejected. It cannot change a rule's answer. Every paragraph needs exactly one answer. |
| Mark a target paragraph as not CSI | Leave a paragraph exactly as it is. | Only one reason is allowed: non_csi_content. An ignored paragraph receives no edits at all. |
| Choose a template's example paragraphs | Say which template paragraph shows each role's formatting. | The formatting itself is copied from that paragraph, never written by the model. Strong text signals overrule it, and the style each one is based on is taken from the template. |
| Name the generated styles | Choose the display name of each CSI_ style it creates. | The name is escaped as plain text. The style's ID is fixed by the app. |
| Write notes about a template | Add free-text remarks to its answer. | Kept only in the template cache's audit file; never in your output or the run records. |
| Tools | None. | No tools are offered, so the model can only reply with text in the required form. |

What the AI categorically cannot do: open, read or write any file; reach the network or any address; run code; see a whole document, a file name, an image, a header or a footer; set a formatting value; change a word of your text; or decide a number. Numbers written by the Canadian-to-CSI conversion are counted by the app from Word's own list.

<a id="terms"></a>

### What the key terms mean, exactly

*Definitions*

#### “Never modified” / “read only”

> **The exact claim:** The app opens your template and targets only to copy them. All work happens on the copy, and each original is fingerprinted again before its output is published.

**What it does not claim:** It does not stop another program, such as Word or a sync client, from changing the file meanwhile. It notices and stops instead.

#### “Verified”

> **The exact claim:** The output passed every automated check for its mode: complete coverage, body text run by run except predicted changes, numbering, tracked changes, indentation, styles read back, and every untouched part byte for byte.

**What it does not claim:** It does not mean the right role was chosen, that every page looks right in Word, or that the specification is technically correct.

#### “Unchanged” (Format only)

> **The exact claim:** Every body paragraph keeps its exact text, including tabs, breaks, spaces, hyphens and tracked deletions, and its effective list numbering.

**What it does not claim:** Headers and footers are replaced by the template's. The page can reflow because fonts, margins and defaults change. The file is not byte-identical.

#### “Deterministic” / “rules”

> **The exact claim:** Decided by fixed code on your computer: the same file always gives the same answer, with no AI and no network.

**What it does not claim:** It does not mean correct. A rule can be confidently wrong, and the AI cannot overrule it.

#### “No document text in the records”

> **The exact claim:** run.json, audit.json, run.log and diagnostics.jsonl carry counts, codes, fingerprints, model names and locations given as a section number and a heading count, never paragraph text, and your key is removed wherever it could appear.

**What it does not claim:** File names and folder paths are recorded. The template cache does keep the first 200 characters of each template paragraph.

#### “Cached”

> **The exact claim:** A template analysis is reused only when the template's fingerprint, the app's engine, the model, the prompts and the format version all match, and every file in it checks out.

**What it does not claim:** The cache never expires. The app does not encrypt it; like your other files it is protected only by your Windows account.

#### “Fail closed”

> **The exact claim:** When the app cannot prove a step, it stops that target and publishes nothing for it, rather than guess.

**What it does not claim:** It does not mean you get a partial result. A refused or failed target still costs whatever requests were already made.

#### “Tokens counted” / “usage”

> **The exact claim:** The counts Anthropic reported in each response, totalled per target and per run. A missing count is marked unknown.

**What it does not claim:** It is not a price and not your invoice; Anthropic's bill is the authority.

<a id="no-ai"></a>

### The parts with no AI in them

*No AI here*

- Copying your files to private snapshots and fingerprinting them.
- Unpacking and checking every Word file against the size and safety limits.
- Reading paragraphs, styles, numbering, headers and footers.
- The rules that label paragraphs from Word's numbering and unmistakable text.
- Choosing which paragraphs need the AI at all.
- Checking every AI answer.
- Copying formatting from the template's example paragraphs.
- Importing styles under private names.
- Applying page layout, headers and footers.
- Both Canadian conversions, including every number written as text.
- The built-in Canadian numbering scheme.
- Every verification check and the decision to publish.
- Publishing outputs and writing run records.
- Checking and reusing cached template analyses.
- The update check and installer fingerprint check.

> **With the network disconnected**
>
> These still work: the whole window and its help; both no-template modes; and a template mode with a template already in the cache. In each case, a target works when rules label every paragraph. What cannot work is analyzing a new template and labelling paragraphs the rules could not settle: those targets fail after their retries, with a record saying so. The update check fails silently.

<a id="security"></a>

### Security and privacy, mechanism by mechanism

*Security*

| Concern | How it is handled |
|---|---|
| Your API key at rest | Held in memory by default. With Remember, stored in Windows Credential Manager under SpecificationFormatter / anthropic-api-key; unticking deletes it. Never written to a file by the app. |
| Your API key in logs and records | Replaced wherever it could appear in run.log, run.json, audit.json, diagnostics.jsonl and on-screen errors. |
| A malicious or damaged Word file | Treated as untrusted. Paths that escape the file, duplicates and links are refused; size is capped at 10,000 entries, 512 MiB, 128 MiB per part and a compression ratio of 1,000 to one. Header and footer images: 16 MiB each, 64 MiB in all. |
| XML tricks (entity expansion) | Any DOCTYPE or ENTITY declaration is refused before the file is parsed, in any text encoding. |
| Links inside a Word file | Recorded, never followed: no internet address, network share or local path named by a document is opened. |
| A tampered update | The version file must arrive over HTTPS, and the installer must match its SHA-256 fingerprint before it can be run. The app is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first install. |
| A tampered or stale template cache | Every cached file is checked against its recorded fingerprint and the profile against the current engine; anything that does not match is ignored. |
| Listening for connections | None. The app runs no server and opens no port. |
| Administrator rights | Not needed. The installer installs for your user only. |
| Data left on disk | Template cache: %LOCALAPPDATA%\SpecificationFormatter\TemplateCache. Update state and downloaded installers: %LOCALAPPDATA%\SpecificationFormatter. Both are plain files protected only by your Windows account, and both survive uninstalling. Delete the folders to remove them; untick Remember first to delete the key. |
| Traffic redirected by settings | ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and SPEC_FORMATTER_UPDATE_URL can point traffic elsewhere; see the boundary section. |

<a id="money"></a>

### What it costs, and who bills you

*Money*

- **Who bills you.** Anthropic, directly, for model use on the API account your key belongs to. The app has no subscription, no server and no share of the spend.
- **What is billed.** The input and output tokens of each model request, including the model's thinking. Anthropic documents its token-counting service as free.
- **When nothing is spent.** When rules label every paragraph, when a template is already cached, and in any run that fails its input checks.
- **What is estimated.** The app never shows a price. Its only estimates are internal limits: a size estimate used to split long targets, and Anthropic's token count, which Anthropic itself calls an estimate.
- **What is exact.** The token counts Anthropic reports in each response, recorded per target in audit.json and per run in run.json (diagnostics.usage). If a count never arrives it is marked unknown and the total is a lower bound.
- **Failed and stopped work.** Requests that finished are billed even if the target then fails or you cancel, and they are counted in the records. An answer cut off by Cancel is recorded as unknown.

- A template is refused before any request above 150,000 input tokens.
- A target with more than 2,000 paragraphs needing the AI is refused before any request.
- Each Haiku request must measure under 95,000 tokens. The code's stated reason is a price step at 100,000 tokens; check Anthropic's pricing page for current rates.
- Retries and follow-up requests are counted limits, listed on the cards above.
- At most 4 requests run at once.

<a id="honesty"></a>

### What this does not do

*Honesty*

- It does not check or revise technical content: codes, standards, references, units, terminology or requirements.
- The AI can give a paragraph the wrong role. The text and numbering checks still pass, so the paragraph gets the wrong style and nothing automated notices. Guard: rules decide first, roles are limited to a fixed list, and you review the output.
- A rule can be confidently wrong, and the AI cannot overrule it. Guard: rules fire only on narrow, unmistakable shapes and leave anything ambiguous to the AI.
- The records do not show which paragraphs the AI labelled, only how many. You cannot trace one AI decision to its paragraph after the run.
- AI answers can differ between two runs of the same file.
- The checks prove the file's structure, not its appearance. Applying a template's page layout and defaults reflows pages, so look at every page in Word.
- In the template modes your headers and footers are replaced by the template's; the section number and title are filled in only where the app can confirm them, otherwise the target fails.
- Tables, text boxes and drawings are not restyled.
- Canadian conversion refuses documents whose numbering it cannot prove, rather than guess. A round trip to Canadian and back drops a dash typed after PART n, so PART 1 - GENERAL returns as PART 1 GENERAL.
- The template cache keeps excerpts of every template it has analyzed, indefinitely, and downloaded installers pile up; uninstalling removes neither.
- The installer is not code-signed. The window has a dark theme only, and the shipped build is for Windows.
- Token counts are not an invoice.

<a id="check"></a>

### Check it yourself

*The point*

From least effort to most. Each says what you will see.

1. Click Open Output Folder and open run.log in Notepad. You will see, for each target, either “Anthropic request skipped” or “Classifying unresolved paragraphs with Anthropic”, the counts of paragraphs decided by rules and sent to the AI, and every part of the file that changed.
2. Open the target's audit.json. You will see its final role for every paragraph, the counts, the tokens used and, for a failure, an error code with a location.
3. Open run.json and search it for your key and for a sentence from your specification. Neither is there. You will see the model IDs, the effort and diagnostics.usage.
4. In PowerShell, run Get-FileHash on your original and compare it with source.sha256 in the audit. They match, and they still match after the run.
5. In Word, use Review › Compare on the original and the Format only output. You will see formatting changes and no inserted or deleted body text.
6. Compare diagnostics.usage in run.json with the Usage page of the Anthropic Console for the same period. Use a key that nothing else uses and the totals should agree; the Console is the bill.
7. Disconnect from the network and run a no-template mode, or a template you have used before. Targets that rules settle fully still finish; others fail with a record.
8. Set SPEC_FORMATTER_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 and click Check for Updates. It says checks are turned off and sends nothing.
9. Watch a firewall log or the Network tab of Windows Resource Monitor. You will see api.anthropic.com only during runs that need AI, and github.com once a day at most, at launch, and whenever you click Check for Updates.
10. Read the source and run its tests: pip install -r requirements-dev.txt, then python -m pytest. The ledger in docs/TRUST_CLAIMS.md names the code behind every claim here.

> **Still not convinced?**
>
> Good. That is the right stance for anything that touches a document with your name on it. Run it on copies first. Start with Format only, the mode that proves your words did not change. Compare every page with the original. Treat every paragraph's style as a draft until you have looked at it, and keep the run folder with the deliverable so the record travels with the file.
